title: Finite and Non-Finite Verbs: An Introduction
content:
## Finite and Non-Finite Verbs: An Introduction

An introduction to finite and non-finite verbs, including their relationship with the subject and examples such as “He plays cricket” and “He wants to play cricket.”

### Understand the pattern

A finite verb heads a finite clause and can express tense or modality. Many finite present forms show subject agreement, as plays does with he. Not every finite verb visibly changes for person: modal can has the same form with I and she.

### Worked answers and explanation

In 'He plays cricket', plays is finite. In 'He wants to play cricket', wants is finite and to play is non-finite. Infinitives and participles can be non-finite: 'Reading quietly, she waited' has the non-finite reading and finite waited. Non-finite forms are not generally called absolute verbs; an absolute construction is a specific different structure.

### Try another

Identify the finite verb: They hope to finish before lunch.

### Suggested answer

Hope is finite and agrees with they. To finish is a non-finite infinitive; it does not independently establish the tense of the sentence.
